messages.content:
Risk: Inadequate observability
Description: The AI system may lack sufficient logging or traceability features, making it difficult to monitor or audit its decision-making process after the fact.
Concern: None
Policy: Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/PartiesAndSituations/SoftwareAgent: software agent — digital entity that perceives its environment and takes actions that maximize its chance of successfully achieving its goals [found by 4/7 queries]
  Siblings: automated underwriting system, automated system, party
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#AlgorithmicDiscrimination: Algorithmic Discrimination — Systematic bias in automated decision-making systems that disadvantages specific groups based on protected characteristics. [found by 3/7 queries]
  Siblings: Employment Discrimination, Discriminatory Denial of Service, Housing Discrimination
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#DeepfakeDisinformation: Deepfake Disinformation — Use of AI-generated synthetic media depicting individuals saying or doing things they did not, created intentionally to deceive and manipulate audiences. [found by 3/7 queries]
  Siblings: State-Sponsored Propaganda, Conspiracy Theory Promotion
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0033071: Impaired task monitoring — Impaired ability to keep track of one's problem-solving success or failure, and to identify and correct mistakes during performance of a goal. [found by 3/7 queries]
  Siblings: Impaired ability to plan, Impaired self monitoring, Impaired ability to organize
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000146: Artificial Language — A Language that is developed through conscious planning and premeditation, rather than one that was developed through use and repetition. [found by 3/7 queries]
  Siblings: Natural Language

axes.rationale: The AI system itself acts as the agent that requires observability for monitoring and auditing its decision-making process.
The risk involves the AI system's inability to monitor its own tasks, which aligns with the concept of impaired task monitoring.
